newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bank to set up $150 mln Euro CD plan.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bank to set up $150 mln Euro CD plan.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque de la Mediterranee said on Thursday it will set up a $150 million Eurodeposit programme through Merrill Lynch International -- the first Euro-CDs to be issued by a Lebanese commercial bank.

Mediterranee, which is owned by billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and is Lebanon's biggest bank in terms of assets, said in a statement it intended to launch the first tranche of the programme this month in the form of a $50 million issue of two-year Euro certificates of deposit.
"The programme will be the first continuous issuance vehicle established by a Lebanese issuer. The size of the programme will be established for the aggregate amount of $150 million," it added.

"It is Mediterranee's intention to establish a benchmark through the first issue, thus enabling it to access the international capital markets for future tranches with maturities ranging from one to five years," the bank said.

The statement did not give the interest rate on the CDs but other Euro debt instruments issued or to be issued by Lebanese banks are priced several basis points over U.S. treasuries of comparable maturity.
The issue will be lead managed by Merrill Lynch International and Mediterranee Investment Bank, the bank's investment arm.
